gloss: to join, to graft, to set (bones)

definitions.explanation: To align broken bones for healing.
To join a part of one plant to another.

examples.japanese: {壊|こわ}れた{板|いた}を{接|つ}いで{直|なお}した。
examples.english: I repaired the broken board by joining the pieces together.

examples.japanese: {短|みじか}い{布|ぬの}を{何枚|なんまい}も{接|つ}いで、{大|おお}きなカーテンを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I joined many short pieces of cloth together to make a large curtain.

examples.japanese: {折|お}れた{骨|ほね}を{接|つ}いでもらった。
examples.english: I had the broken bone set.

examples.japanese: {接骨院|せっこついん}で{指|ゆび}の{骨|ほね}を{接|つ}いでもらったら、すぐに{楽|らく}になった。
examples.english: When I had my finger bone set at the bonesetting clinic, it felt better right away.

examples.japanese: {果物|くだもの}の{木|き}を{接|つ}いで{新|あたら}しい{品種|ひんしゅ}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Create new varieties by grafting fruit trees.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{枝|えだ}を{別|べつ}の{木|き}に{接|つ}いで{育|そだ}てている。
examples.english: I am growing cherry blossoms by grafting branches onto another tree.

notes:
{接|つ}ぐ means to join, connect, or set (bones), typically connecting separate pieces.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を for the object being joined

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {骨|ほね}を{接|つ}ぐ: to set bones
- {木|き}を{接|つ}ぐ: to graft trees
- {切|き}れた{部分|ぶぶん}を{接|つ}ぐ: to join broken parts

KANJI DISTINCTION (homophones):
- {接|つ}ぐ: to join, connect, set bones, graft
- {注|つ}ぐ: to pour (liquid)
- {継|つ}ぐ: to succeed, inherit, continue
- {次|つ}ぐ: to rank next to

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- {接骨|せっこつ}: bonesetting
- {接骨院|せっこついん}: bonesetting clinic
- {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}: grafting (horticulture)
